notes: Correct for both zip and squashfs: suffix is applied before root matching, NewObject verifies the returned remote so it agrees with List, link targets come from StatT, and it also handles single-file roots and out-of-range seeks; tests are thorough, though NewObject's fallback logic is a bit convoluted.
Implementation matches the reference exactly, with focused zip and squashfs tests, an end-to-end hostile-archive escape test, and a relevant docs section; range/seek reads of links are not tested.

Works for the main flows, but LinkRemote leaves a symlink already ending in .rclonelink unsuffixed, so it collides with a regular member of that name and copies under the wrong name; zip reads every symlink body at mount time even without --links; using obj.Remote() for squashfs f.file risks breaking single-file roots; new shared helpers widen the change.

Reads config from context.Background(), so per-context --links is ignored (0/3 hidden tests); Size() decompresses the link on every call; squashfs reads links via OpenFile; tests mutate global config; the patch commits a binary and several debug shell scripts with absolute local paths.

Squashfs reads links through OpenFile and uses item.Size(), and NewObject always strips the suffix, which breaks regular .rclonelink members; validateSymlinkTarget wrongly rejects legitimate ../ and absolute targets; a racy process-global notice flag is used, code has gofmt whitespace issues, and no tests were added.

Zip listing and reading work, but squashfs NewObject strips the suffix and retries with allowSymlink=true, so NewObject("file.txt.rclonelink") returns the regular file.txt and listing and lookup disagree; the extra zip logic that silently drops members under symlinks is unrequested, and a root pointing at a suffixed link is not resolved.
